root_cause.text: In `drm_buddy_alloc_blocks()` the rounded-up allocation size for contiguous or large-min-block requests was not validated against `mm->size`, allowing oversized requests to proceed until `order > mm->max_order` and hit a `BUG_ON`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early check `if (order > mm->max_order || size > mm->size)` before the existing `BUG_ON(order > mm->max_order)`, and the CVE description says `roundup_pow_of_two()` / `round_up()` can make `size` exceed `mm->size`, which “later triggers BUG_ON(order > mm->max_order)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject oversized buddy allocations early, while preserving a fallback attempt for contiguous requests.
intent_record.what: In drm_buddy_alloc_blocks(), a new early check was added after computing order and min_order: if the requested order exceeds mm->max_order or the requested size exceeds mm->size, the function now either calls __alloc_contig_try_harder() when DRM_BUDDY_CONTIGUOUS_ALLOCATION is set without DRM_BUDDY_RANGE_ALLOCATION, or returns -EINVAL otherwise.
intent_record.how: This prevents the normal allocation path from proceeding with requests that are larger than the buddy allocator can satisfy, avoiding invalid allocation attempts. For contiguous allocations, it preserves a fallback path that retries with a different strategy instead of failing immediately.

grouping_result.intent: Reject oversized buddy allocations early, while preserving a fallback attempt for contiguous requests.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it adds early rejection of oversized buddy allocations before they can reach the invalid `order > mm->max_order` path and trigger the `BUG_ON`, while still allowing the contiguous fallback behavior.

candidates.rationale: This computes the allocation order from the requested page count without any prior validation against mm->size. For oversized requests, the derived order can exceed the buddy allocator limits and later trigger the BUG_ON.

This derives the minimum block order from the requested minimum block size, but before the fix there was no check that the rounded-up size was within mm->size. Large requests could therefore propagate into invalid order handling.

This re-clamps the order inside the allocation loop, but it still operates after the oversized request has already been accepted. The root cause is the missing early bounds check, which allows the code to reach the later BUG_ON path.

This is the crash point reached when an oversized request was not rejected early enough. The vulnerable behavior manifests here because invalid requests are allowed to continue until this assertion fires.

vuln_statements.explanation: This computes the allocation order from the requested page count before any validation against mm->size, allowing oversized requests to proceed into invalid order handling.
This derives the minimum block order from the requested minimum block size without first ensuring the rounded-up allocation fits within mm->size, so oversized requests can propagate further.
This re-clamps the order only after the oversized request has already been accepted, so it does not prevent the later BUG_ON path from being reached.
This is the crash point triggered when an oversized request is not rejected early enough; the vulnerability manifests when invalid requests reach this assertion.
